title: Astrid and the Cipher
premise: Ada Nystrom, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, has spent three years in the coastal town of Greywater keeping everyone's secrets filed and alphabetized—including her own. When a drowned man washes up wearing clothes stolen from her closet, she realizes someone is framing the one person who trusts her: her estranged brother Elias, officially dead for a decade. Following a cipher hidden in old insurance claims their father left behind, Ada uncovers that Elias faked his death to escape a smuggling ring now run by the town's beloved harbormaster—and that her own missing memories of the night he 'died' hold the key. In the end, Ada chooses truth over loyalty, testifying against the ring at the cost of her brother's freedom and her anonymity, but winning back the self she buried with the past.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years cataloguing losses along the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet Ada filing claims in her immaculate office, establishing her photographic memory and her rule of never knowing more than the job requires. A routine drowning claim arrives from Greywater Cove. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the comfort of order.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The body wears her own missing cardigan and scarf—items stolen from her closet weeks ago. Police treat her as a suspect; her perfect memory becomes a liability when she can't account for one evening. Emotional beat: fear cracking open her carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Elias, Deceased Ten Years
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback threads. The victim is identified as a stranger, but his fingerprints match files from a decade-old case—the year her brother Elias supposedly drowned. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as suspicion.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Harbormaster Soren Voss POV. Charming, respected Soren offers Ada help and quiet warnings about digging into old cases. Readers glimpse his menace beneath warmth. Emotional beat: dread disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Searching the cove where Elias died, she finds a rusted lockbox containing insurance claim forms bearing her father's signature and a string of numbers. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Photographic Gaps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her flawless memory has a hole—the night Elias vanished. She realizes someone drugged her, and begins reconstructing the missing hours from physical evidence instead. Emotional beat: violation and resolve.

chapters.title: The Cipher in Claim 4471
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Decoding her father's numbers reveals they index policy numbers pointing to cargo shipments that never existed—ghost freight used to launder smuggled goods. Emotional beat: intellectual thrill, first real hope.

chapters.title: An Old Friend's Debt
chapters.summary: Mira, the tavern owner and Ada's only friend, POV. Mira admits she saw Elias alive two years ago and was paid by Voss to stay silent. Her guilt over deceiving Ada fractures their friendship. Emotional beat: betrayal inside loyalty.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the cipher to a decommissioned lighthouse, she finds signs someone lives there—her brother's handwriting on ration lists. Elias is alive and hiding. Emotional beat: vertiginous joy shadowed by anger.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Elias POV. His account of faking his death after witnessing a dock murder, and why he let Ada believe he was gone—to keep Voss from using her. Emotional beat: love expressed as abandonment.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She confronts Elias at the lighthouse; he refuses to testify, insisting the only other witness—a customs officer named Halloran—died with the truth. Ada suspects otherwise. Emotional beat: fury and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Soren Voss POV. He invites Ada to dinner, revealing he knows she's found the cipher, and offers her father's old debts as leverage: leave town, and Elias stays free. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: Halloran's Widow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Tracking the 'dead' witness, Ada finds Halloran's widow living under a new name two towns over—and learns the officer himself may have escaped the same way Elias did. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Fire at the Records Office
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Arson destroys the county archives, erasing the original claims. Ada's memory is now the only copy of the evidence—which makes her the most dangerous witness alive. Emotional beat: terror of being indispensable.

chapters.title: Alphabetized and Burned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Under police protection that feels like custody, Ada recites the decoded ledger from memory for a skeptical detective, Rask, who quietly believes her but warns that Voss owns half the force. Emotional beat: isolation deepening into unlikely alliance.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Rask POV. Halloran's widow is found drowned—wearing Elias's old jacket. The killer is staging deaths from the siblings' pasts, tightening the frame. Emotional beat: the noose closing.

chapters.title: What Ada Forgot
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Reconstructing the drugged night, Ada remembers: she saw Voss on the dock ten years ago, and her father helped cover it up to protect her testimony from being used. Her inheritance was complicity. Emotional beat: devastation of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Brother Against Tide
chapters.summary: Elias POV. Voss captures Elias, offering a trade: the cipher's final page for Ada's silence. Elias escapes wounded and runs to warn her, choosing her safety over his own at last. Emotional beat: redemption through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With a storm closing the harbor, Ada decodes the final entry: the location of the ring's current shipment and the original murder weapon, both aboard Voss's flagship. She must act tonight or lose everything. Emotional beat: cold clarity before the plunge.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Up What It Took
chapters.summary: Ada and Rask POV, alternating. Climax aboard the flagship during the storm: Ada confronts Voss, trading her testimony for Elias's release while Rask records the confession and seizes the cargo. Voss is arrested as the storm breaks. Emotional beat: courage answering fear.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At trial, Ada speaks every secret she ever filed away, including her father's cover-up and her own erased night. Elias accepts a reduced sentence for obstruction; forgiveness begins across a courtroom table. Emotional beat: truth costing everything and giving back the self.

chapters.title: A New System of Order
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. A year later, Ada leaves insurance work, opens a small archive consultancy helping families recover lost records, and visits Elias on release weekends. The tide comes in clean. Emotional beat: peace earned, not arranged.
